claim: Deletion of two diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases VIH1/2 impairs plant growth.
source: Here we report that deletion of two diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases VIH1/2 impairs plant growth and leads to constitutive Pi starvation responses.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, and it is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Deletion of VIH1/2 leads to constitutive Pi starvation responses.
source: Here we report that deletion of two diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases VIH1/2 impairs plant growth and leads to constitutive Pi starvation responses.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by gene expression data in Figure 1G.

claim: Deletion of phosphate starvation response transcription factors partially rescues vih1 vih2 mutant phenotypes.
source: Deletion of phosphate starvation response transcription factors partially rescues vih1 vih2 mutant phenotypes, placing diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases in plant Pi signal transduction cascades.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 3 shows the genetic interaction data.

claim: VIH1/2 are bifunctional enzymes able to generate and break-down PP-InsPs.
source: VIH1/2 are bifunctional enzymes able to generate and break-down PP-InsPs.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 5 provides biochemical assay data demonstrating both kinase and phosphatase activities.

claim: Mutations in the kinase active site lead to increased Pi levels and constitutive Pi starvation responses.
source: Mutations in the kinase active site lead to increased Pi levels and constitutive Pi starvation responses.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: ATP levels change significantly in different Pi growth conditions.
source: ATP levels change significantly in different Pi growth conditions.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 6D shows ATP/ADP measurements under different Pi conditions.

claim: ATP-Mg2+ concentrations shift the relative kinase and phosphatase activities of diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases in vitro.
source: ATP-Mg2+ concentrations shift the relative kinase and phosphatase activities of diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 6A-B show in vitro enzyme assays with varying ATP-Mg2+ concentrations.

claim: Pi inhibits the phosphatase activity of the enzyme.
source: Pi inhibits the phosphatase activity of the enzyme.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2 shows phosphatase activity assays in the presence of Pi.

claim: VIH1 and VIH2 relay changes in cellular ATP and Pi concentrations to changes in PP-InsP levels, allowing plants to maintain sufficient Pi levels.
source: Thus, VIH1 and VIH2 relay changes in cellular ATP and Pi concentrations to changes in PP-InsP levels, allowing plants to maintain sufficient Pi levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations including ATP/ADP measurements, enzyme kinetics, and genetic analyses.

claim: Many eukaryotic proteins regulating phosphate (Pi) homeostasis contain SPX domains that are receptors for inositol pyrophosphates (PP-InsP).
source: Many eukaryotic proteins regulating phosphate (Pi) homeostasis contain SPX domains that are receptors for inositol pyrophosphates (PP-InsP), suggesting that PP-InsPs may regulate Pi homeostasis.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work (Wild et al., 2016).

claim: Plants can take up phosphite (Phi), a reduced form of Pi which however cannot be used as a source of phosphorus.
source: Plants can also take up phosphite (Phi), a reduced form of Pi which however cannot be used as a source of phosphorus (Ticconi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Ticconi et al., 2001.

claim: SPX domains act as cellular receptors for inositol pyrophosphate (PP-InsP) signaling molecules.
source: We have previously shown that these domains act as cellular receptors for inositol pyrophosphate (PP-InsP) signaling molecules (Wild et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors, with citation.

claim: PP-InsPs are composed of a fully phosphorylated inositol ring containing one or two pyrophosphate moieties.
source: PP-InsPs are composed of a fully phosphorylated inositol ring containing one or two pyrophosphate moieties (Shears, 2018).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citation to Shears, 2018.

claim: PP-InsPs bind to a basic surface cluster highly conserved among SPX domains to regulate diverse biochemical and cellular processes in fungi, plants and animals.
source: PP-InsPs bind to a basic surface cluster highly conserved among SPX domains to regulate divers biochemical and cellular processes in fungi, plants and animals
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations describing various SPX domain functions.

claim: The N-terminal SPX domains of the yeast VTC complex stimulates its inorganic polyphosphate polymerase activity when bound to 5PP-InsP5.
source: The N-terminal SPX domains of the yeast VTC complex stimulates its inorganic polyphosphate polymerase activity when bound to 5PP-InsP5 (Hothorn et al., 2009; Wild et al., 2016; Gerasimaite et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Mutations in the PP-InsP binding surfaces of N-terminal SPX domains of plant and human phosphate exporters affect their Pi transport activities.
source: In plant and human phosphate exporters, mutations in the PP-InsP binding surfaces of their N-terminal SPX domains affect their Pi transport activities (Legati et al., 2015; Wild et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Plants contain additional soluble, stand-alone SPX proteins, which have been shown to bind PHOSPHATE STARVATION RESPONSE (PHR) transcription factors.
source: Plants contain additional soluble, stand-alone SPX proteins, which have been shown to bind PHOSPHATE STARVATION RESPONSE (PHR) transcription factors (Rubio et al., 2001; Puga et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014; Qi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: PHR1 and its homolog PHL1 are master regulators of the plant Pi starvation response.
source: PHR1 and its homolog PHL1 are master regulators of the plant Pi starvation response, which enable plants to grow and survive in Pi limiting growth conditions (Bustos et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Bustos et al., 2010.

claim: PP-InsP-bound SPX domains can physically interact with PHR1, keeping it from binding DNA.
source: PP-InsP-bound SPX domains can physically interact with PHR1, keeping it from binding DNA (Puga et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014; Wild et al., 2016; Qi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: In the absence of PP-InsPs, the SPX – PHR1 complex dissociates and PHR1 oligomers can target the promoters of Pi starvation induced (PSI) genes.
source: In the absence of PP-InsPs, the SPX – PHR1 complex dissociates and PHR1 oligomers can target the promoters of Pi starvation induced (PSI) genes, resulting in major changes in plant metabolism and development (Wild et al., 2016; Jung et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: 5PP-InsP5 levels are reduced in yeast and in animal cells grown in Pi starvation conditions.
source: 5PP-InsP5 levels are indeed reduced in yeast and in animal cells grown in Pi starvation conditions (Lonetti et al., 2011; Wild et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2017a)
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: PP-InsP metabolic enzymes may be key regulators of Pi homeostasis.
source: suggesting that PP-InsP metabolic enzymes may be key regulators of Pi homeostasis (Gu et al., 2017a; Azevedo and Saiardi, 2017; Shears, 2018).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: Inositol hexakisphosphate kinases Kcs1/IP6K catalyze the synthesis of 5PP-InsP5 from InsP6.
source: PP-InsP biosynthesis is well understood in yeast and mammals, where inositol hexakisphosphate kinases Kcs1/IP6K catalyze the synthesis of 5PP-InsP5 from InsP6.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 5PP-InsP5 can be further phosphorylated by diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases Vip1/PPIP5K to 1,5(PP)2-InsP4 (referred to as InsP8 in this study).
source: 5PP-InsP5 can be further phosphorylated by diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases Vip1/PPIP5K to 1,5(PP)2-InsP4 (referred to as InsP8 in this study) (Shears, 2018) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated with citation and reference to a figure showing the pathway.

claim: Kcs1/IP6Ks have a Km for ATP in the low millimolar range and may therefore generate 5PP-InsP5 in response to changes in cellular ATP levels.
source: Currently, it is known that Kcs1/IP6Ks have a Km for ATP in the low millimolar range and may therefore generate 5PP-InsP5 in response to changes in cellular ATP levels (Saiardi et al., 1999; Gu et al., 2017a; Gu et al., 2017b).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Human PPIP5Ks can be regulated by Pi itself, stimulating their 5PP-InsP5 kinase activity, and inhibiting their InsP8 phosphatase activity.
source: In addition, human PPIP5Ks can be regulated by Pi itself, stimulating their 5PP-InsP5 kinase activity, and inhibiting their InsP8 phosphatase activity (Gu et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Gu et al., 2017a.

claim: Vip1/PPIP5Ks are bifunctional enzymes harboring an N-terminal InsP kinase and a C-terminal phosphatase domain.
source: Vip1/PPIP5Ks are bifunctional enzymes harboring an N-terminal InsP kinase and a C-terminal phosphatase domain (Figure 1A) (Mulugu et al., 2007; Fridy et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations and reference to Figure 1A showing domain architecture.

claim: The yeast and animal kinase domain acts on the phosphate group at the C1 position of the inositol ring of both InsP6 and 5PP-InsP5, yielding 1PP-InsP5 or InsP8 reaction products.
source: The yeast and animal kinase domain acts on the phosphate group at the C1 position of the inositol ring of both InsP6 and 5PP-InsP5, yielding 1PP-InsP5 or InsP8 reaction products (Mulugu et al., 2007; Fridy et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: The phosphatase domain has been characterized as a specific 1PP-InsP5 / InsP8 phosphatase in yeast.
source: The phosphatase domain has been characterized as a specific 1PP-InsP5 / InsP8 phosphatase in yeast (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Wang et al., 2015.

claim: Deletion of PPIP5K in human cells results in lower InsP8 and elevated ATP levels, due to enhanced mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and increased glycolysis.
source: Deletion of PPIP5K in human cells results in lower InsP8 and elevated ATP levels, due to enhanced mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and increased glycolysis (Gu et al., 2017b).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Gu et al., 2017b.

claim: No IP6K enzyme has been identified in plants thus far.
source: In plants, no IP6K enzyme has been identified thus far, but Vip1/PPIP5K orthologs Vip1 and VIH1/2 have been reported from Chlamydomonas (Couso et al., 2016) and Arabidopsis (Desai et al., 2014; Laha et al., 2015), respectively.
evidence: This is stated as current knowledge with citations.

claim: Vip1/PPIP5K orthologs Vip1 and VIH1/2 have been reported from Chlamydomonas and Arabidopsis.
source: In plants, no IP6K enzyme has been identified thus far, but Vip1/PPIP5K orthologs Vip1 and VIH1/2 have been reported from Chlamydomonas (Couso et al., 2016) and Arabidopsis (Desai et al., 2014; Laha et al., 2015), respectively.
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: The algal and plant enzymes share the bifunctional kinase/phosphatase domain architecture with yeast and animal PPIP5Ks.
source: The algal and plant enzymes share the bifunctional kinase/phosphatase domain architecture with yeast and animal PPIP5Ks.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison based on known structures.

claim: Arabidopsis VIH1 and VIH2 can rescue yeast vip1 but not ksc1 mutants.
source: Arabidopsis VIH1 and VIH2 can rescue yeast vip1 but not ksc1 mutants (Desai et al., 2014; Laha et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Deletion of the Chlamydomonas Vip1 results in nutrient signaling phenotypes affecting carbon metabolism.
source: Deletion of the Chlamydomonas Vip1 results in nutrient signaling phenotypes affecting carbon metabolism (Couso et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Couso et al., 2016.

claim: The Arabidopsis vih2-4 loss-of-function mutant has lower InsP8 but increased InsP7 levels.
source: The Arabidopsis vih2-4 loss-of-function mutant has lower InsP8 but increased InsP7 levels, suggesting that the enzyme may generate an InsP8 isoform in vivo (Laha et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Laha et al., 2015.

claim: VIH2 mutant lines have been reported to affect jasmonic acid-regulated herbivore resistance, as PP-InsPs also form critical co-factors of the jasmonate receptor complex.
source: VIH2 mutant lines have been reported to affect jasmonic acid-regulated herbivore resistance, as PP-InsPs also form critical co-factors of the jasmonate receptor complex (Sheard et al., 2010; Laha et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: No obvious Pi starvation phenotype has been reported for vih2 mutants.
source: No obvious Pi starvation phenotype has been reported for these mutants (Kuo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Kuo et al., 2018.

claim: Arabidopsis VIH1 and VIH2 show 89% sequence identity at the protein level.
source: Arabidopsis VIH1 and VIH2 show 89% sequence identity at the protein level (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to a sequence alignment figure.

claim: VIH1 has been previously reported to be specifically expressed in pollen while VIH2 showed a broad expression pattern as judged from qRT-PCR experiments.
source: VIH1 has been previously reported to be specifically expressed in pollen while VIH2 showed a broad expression pattern as judged from qRT-PCR experiments (Desai et al., 2014; Laha et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: VIH2 is expressed in different tissues and organs, and VIH1 shows strong expression in pollen.
source: We found VIH2 to be expressed in different tissues and organs, and strong expression for VIH1 in pollen as previously reported (Laha et al., 2016) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated with reference to GUS reporter line data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: VIH1 shows additional expression in root tips, where VIH2 is also expressed.
source: However, our GUS lines reveal additional expression of VIH1 in root tips, where also VIH2 is expressed (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated with reference to GUS reporter line data.

claim: VIH1 is expressed in pollen grains, pollen tubes and in the root tip, where VIH2 is also present.
source: VIH1 and VIH2 reporter lines harboring a C-terminal mCitrine (mCit) tag (which complements the vih1 vih2 mutant phenotype, compare Figure 2A, see below) reveal that VIH1 is expressed in pollen grains, pollen tubes and in the root tip, where VIH2 is also present (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated with reference to fluorescent reporter data.

claim: VIH1 and VIH2 show partially overlapping expression in different tissues and organs and both enzymes are localized in the cytoplasm.
source: Thus, VIH1 and VIH2 show partially overlapping expression in different tissues and organs and both enzymes are localized in the cytoplasm (Figure 1—figure supplement 4; compare Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to reporter line data.

claim: vih1-2 vih2-4 and vih1-6 vih2-4 double mutants displayed severe growth phenotypes, while vih1 and vih2 single mutants and vih1 vih2-6 double mutants looked similar to wild-type plants.
source: We found that vih1-2 vih2-4 and vih1-6 vih2-4 double mutants displayed severe growth phenotypes, while vih1 and vih2 single mutants and vih1 vih2-6 double mutants looked similar to wild-type plants (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1C showing plant growth phenotypes.

claim: The VIH2 kinase domain is still expressed in the vih2-6 mutant background, and thus vih2-6 does not represent a full knock-out.
source: The VIH2 kinase domain is still expressed in the vih2-6 mutant background, and thus vih2-6 does not represent a full knock-out (see below, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to RT-PCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: vih2-4 plants expressing an inducible artificial microRNA (amiRNA) targeting the VIH1 transcript show intermediate growth phenotypes.
source: Next, we found that vih2-4 plants expressing an inducible artificial microRNA (amiRNA) targeting the VIH1 transcript show intermediate growth phenotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 5 showing inducible knockdown data.

claim: At seedling stage, the vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant displayed a severe growth phenotype, while vih1-2, vih2-4 and ipk1-1 looked more similar to wild-type.
source: At seedling stage, the vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant displayed a severe growth phenotype, while vih1-2, vih2-4 and ipk1-1 looked more similar to wild-type (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1D showing seedling phenotypes.

claim: While wild-type, vih1-2, vih2-4 and ipk1-1 seedlings showed a decrease in root length in response to Pi limitation, vih1-2 vih2-4 showed the opposite trend.
source: Interestingly, while wild-type, vih1-2, vih2-4 and ipk1-1 seedlings showed a decrease in root length in response to Pi limitation, vih1-2 vih2-4 showed the opposite trend (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1E showing root length measurements.

claim: VIH1 and VIH2 act redundantly in Arabidopsis PP-InsP metabolism.
source: Taken together, independent genetic experiments suggest that VIH1 and VIH2 act redundantly in Arabidopsis PP-InsP metabolism, and that simultaneous loss-of-function of these conserved enzymes strongly affects plant growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple genetic experiments showing that double mutants have severe phenotypes while single mutants do not.

claim: Simultaneous loss-of-function of VIH1 and VIH2 strongly affects plant growth.
source: Taken together, independent genetic experiments suggest that VIH1 and VIH2 act redundantly in Arabidopsis PP-InsP metabolism, and that simultaneous loss-of-function of these conserved enzymes strongly affects plant growth.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from genetic data.

claim: Cellular Pi levels are significantly increased in vih1-2 vih2-4 and in ipk1-1 seedlings in Pi-deficient medium supplemented with either 1 mM or 10 mM Pi, but not in vih1 or vih2 single mutants, when compared to wild-type.
source: In Pi-deficient medium supplemented with either 1 mM or 10 mM Pi, we found cellular Pi levels to be significantly increased in vih1-2 vih2-4 and in ipk1-1 seedlings (Kuo et al., 2014), but not in vih1 or vih2 single mutants, when compared to wild-type (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1F showing Pi content measurements.

claim: In the 10 mM Pi condition, the vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant accumulated significantly more Pi also when compared to ipk1-1.
source: In the 10 mM Pi condition, the vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant accumulated significantly more Pi also when compared to ipk1-1.
evidence: This is stated as a result from Pi content measurements.

claim: Estradiol-induced expression of an amiRNA targeting the VIH1 transcript in the vih2-4 single mutant background led to a significant increase in shoot Pi content when compared to the non-induced control.
source: In a genetically independent experiment, estradiol-induced expression of an amiRNA targeting the VIH1 transcript in the vih2-4 single mutant background also led to a significant increase in shoot Pi content when compared to the non-induced control (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 5 showing inducible knockdown data.

claim: The increase in cellular Pi in vih1-2 vih2-4 plants may be due to the double mutant lacking a VIH1 and VIH2-generated PP-InsP isoform critically involved in Pi homeostasis and starvation responses.
source: We hypothesized that the increase in cellular Pi in vih1-2 vih2-4 plants may be due to the double mutant lacking a VIH1 and VIH2-generated PP-InsP isoform critically involved in Pi homeostasis and starvation responses (Wild et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on previous work and current observations.

claim: PSI marker genes were constitutively expressed in vih1-2 vih2-4 seedlings grown in Pi sufficient (1 mM, 10 mM) growth conditions.
source: Consistently, we found PSI gene expression misregulated in the vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant (Figure 1G). PSI marker genes were constitutively expressed in vih1-2 vih2-4 seedlings grown in Pi sufficient (1 mM, 10 mM) growth conditions (Figure 1G)
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1G showing qRT-PCR data.

claim: The negative regulation of PHR1/PHL1 by PP-InsP-bound SPX domains is compromised in vih1-2 vih2-4 mutants.
source: suggesting that the negative regulation of PHR1/PHL1 by PP-InsP-bound SPX domains is compromised (Wild et al., 2016; Qi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the gene expression data, supported by citations.

claim: VIH1 and VIH2-generated PP-InsPs are implicated in Pi homeostasis and starvation responses.
source: Together, these experiments implicate VIH1 and VIH2-generated PP-InsPs in Pi homeostasis and starvation responses.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the genetic and biochemical data.

claim: Expression of wild-type VIH1 and VIH2 from their endogenous promoters rescued the growth phenotype, cellular Pi content and PSI gene expression of the vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant at seedling stage.
source: At seedling stage, expression of wild-type VIH1 and VIH2 from their endogenous promoters rescued the growth phenotype, cellular Pi content and PSI gene expression of the double mutant (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2A-D showing complementation data.

claim: Expression of a VIH2KD/AA version containing point-mutations in the kinase domain could not complement vih1-2 vih2-4.
source: We could not complement vih1-2 vih2-4 with constructs expressing a VIH2KD/AA version containing point-mutations in the kinase domain (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2A-D showing complementation data.

claim: Expression of a construct harboring point mutations in the VIH2 phosphatase domain (VIH2RH/AA) complemented vih1-2 vih2-4-related phenotypes.
source: In contrast, expression of a construct harboring point mutations in the VIH2 phosphatase domain (VIH2RH/AA) complemented vih1-2 vih2-4-related phenotypes (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2A-D showing complementation data.

claim: vih2-6 results in a shortened transcript, which may encode a truncated version of VIH2 harboring the PPIK5K kinase domain only.
source: We found that vih2-6 results in a shortened transcript, which may encode a truncated version of VIH2 harboring the PPIK5K kinase domain only (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1 showing RT-PCR data.

claim: No phenotypes significantly different from the Col-0 wild-type control plants were observed for the vih2-6 allele at seedling stage.
source: No phenotypes significantly different from the Col-0 wild-type control plants were observed for the vih2-6 allele at seedling stage (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2A-D.

claim: VIH2RH/AA complementation lines and the vih2-6 mutant displayed a significantly reduced shoot Pi content when compared to wild-type in soil-grown adult plants.
source: However, when we re-performed our analyses on soil-grown adult plants, we found that our VIH2RH/AA complementation lines and the vih2-6 mutant displayed a significantly reduced shoot Pi content when compared to wild-type (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2 showing Pi content data.

claim: vih2-6 phenotypes were rescued by expressing wild-type VIH2 in the vih2-6 mutant background.
source: vih2-6 phenotypes were rescued by expressing wild-type VIH2 in the vih2-6 mutant background (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2 showing complementation data.

claim: VIH2KD/AA seedlings showed significantly increased cellular Pi levels, while VIH2RH/AA contained less Pi when grown in Pi sufficient conditions.
source: We found that VIH2KD/AA seedlings showed significantly increased cellular Pi levels, while VIH2RH/AA contained less Pi when grown in Pi sufficient conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3 showing overexpression data.

claim: Plants over-expressing wild-type VIH2 had Pi levels similar to Col-0 control seedlings.
source: Plants over-expressing wild-type VIH2 had Pi levels similar to Col-0 control seedlings (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: PSI target gene expression was found misregulated in both VIH2KD/AA and VIH2RH/AA over-expression lines.
source: PSI target gene expression was found misregulated in both VIH2KD/AA and VIH2RH/AA over-expression lines (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3 showing qRT-PCR data.

claim: At adult stage, mutations in the kinase and phosphatase domains of VIH1 and VIH2 all lead to visible growth phenotypes, with plants having smaller rosette leaves.
source: At adult stage, mutations in the kinase and phosphatase domains of VIH1 and VIH2 all lead to visible growth phenotypes, with plants having smaller rosette leaves (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4 showing plant phenotypes.

claim: The shoot Pi content in VIH1KD/AA and VIH2KD/AA plants was significantly increased compared to wild-type.
source: The shoot Pi content in VIH1KD/AA and VIH2KD/AA plants was significantly increased compared to wild-type (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4 showing Pi content data.

claim: The Pi content of the VIH1RH/AA and VIH2RH/AA lines appeared similar to the Col-0 control when plants were grown in soil.
source: The Pi content of the VIH1RH/AA and VIH2RH/AA lines appeared however similar to the Col-0 control when plants were grown in soil (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The VIH kinase domain has an essential role in plant Pi homeostasis.
source: Taken together, our complementation and overexpression analyses reveal an essential role for the VIH kinase domain, while we speculate that the VIH phosphatase domain may have a regulatory function in plant Pi homeostasis and signaling.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from complementation and overexpression data.

claim: The VIH phosphatase domain may have a regulatory function in plant Pi homeostasis and signaling.
source: Taken together, our complementation and overexpression analyses reveal an essential role for the VIH kinase domain, while we speculate that the VIH phosphatase domain may have a regulatory function in plant Pi homeostasis and signaling.
evidence: This is stated as speculation based on the data.

claim: At seedling stage vih1-2 vih2-4 phr1 phl1 quadruple mutants partially rescue the seedling growth phenotype of vih1-2 vih2-4.
source: We found that at seedling stage vih1-2 vih2-4 phr1 phl1 quadruple mutants partially rescue the seedling growth phenotype of vih1-2 vih2-4 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3A showing seedling phenotypes.

claim: Cellular Pi levels are significantly increased in the vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant and significantly reduced in the phr1 phl1 double mutant when compared to the Col-0 wild-type control.
source: Cellular Pi levels are significantly increased in the vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant (see above) and significantly reduced in the phr1 phl1 double mutant (Bustos et al., 2010) when compared to the Col-0 wild-type control (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3B showing Pi content data and citation to Bustos et al., 2010.

claim: The vih1-2 vih2-4 root growth phenotype under different Pi regimes is restored in the quadruple mutant.
source: The vih1-2 vih2-4 root growth phenotype under different Pi regimes (compare Figure 1E, see above) is restored in the quadruple mutant (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3C showing root length data.

claim: The high PSI gene expression observed for vih1-2 vih2-4 plants in Pi sufficient growth conditions is suppressed in the quadruple mutant.
source: As expected, the high PSI gene expression observed for vih1-2 vih2-4 plants in Pi sufficient growth conditions is suppressed in the quadruple mutant (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3D showing qRT-PCR data.

claim: A partial rescue of the vih1-2 vih2-4 growth phenotype was observed for the quadruple mutant also at later developmental stages, with Pi shoot contents being significantly increased compared to the Col-0 wild-type control.
source: A partial rescue of the vih1-2 vih2-4 growth phenotype was observed for the quadruple mutant also at later developmental stages, with Pi shoot contents being significantly increased compared to the Col-0 wild-type control (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1 showing adult plant data.

claim: Higher amounts of InsP7 isoforms were observed in vih1-2 vih2-4 and vih1-2 vih2-4 phr1 phl1 mutant plants when compared to wild-type, while InsP8 isoforms were no longer detectable.
source: We observed higher amounts of InsP7 isoforms in our double and quadruple mutant plants when compared to wild-type, while InsP8 isoforms were no longer detectable (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3E showing HPLC profiles.

claim: Quantification of the InsP7/InsP6 ratios revealed significantly higher InsP7 levels in the vih1-2 vih2-4 double and vih1-2 vih2-4 phr1 phl1 quadruple mutant.
source: Quantification of the InsP7/InsP6 ratios revealed significantly higher InsP7 levels in the double and quadruple mutant (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3F showing quantification data.

claim: Quantification of the InsP8/InsP7 ratios supports the notion that InsP8 isoforms are not detectable in vih1-2 vih2-4 and vih1-2 vih2-4 phr1 phl1 mutants.
source: Quantification of the InsP8/InsP7 ratios supports the notion that InsP8 isoforms are not detectable in our vih1-2 vih2-4 and vih1-2 vih2-4 phr1 phl1 mutants (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3G showing quantification data.

claim: VIH1/VIH2 and PHR1/PHL1 are part of a common genetic pathway.
source: Taken together, our genetic and metabolic analyses suggest that VIH1/VIH2 and PHR1/PHL1 are part of a common genetic pathway and that in our double and quadruple mutants the InsP8 signaling molecule is not detectable.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from genetic epistasis and metabolite data.

claim: In vih1-2 vih2-4 and vih1-2 vih2-4 phr1 phl1 mutants the InsP8 signaling molecule is not detectable.
source: Taken together, our genetic and metabolic analyses suggest that VIH1/VIH2 and PHR1/PHL1 are part of a common genetic pathway and that in our double and quadruple mutants the InsP8 signaling molecule is not detectable.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from HPLC data.

claim: VIH1 and VIH2 promoter activities do not change significantly in low to high Pi growth conditions.
source: We generated pVIH2::H(istone)2b-mCit lines, which accumulate the fluorescence signal in the nucleus, in either wild-type or vih2-4 mutant background and found no significant changes in promoter activity in low to high Pi growth conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1 showing reporter data.

claim: The known PSI targets SPX1 and SPX3 are highly induced under Pi starvation.
source: In contrast, the known PSI targets SPX1 and SPX3 are highly induced under Pi starvation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) (Duan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and citation to Duan et al., 2008.

claim: GUS reporter lines show slightly reduced VIH1 and VIH2 promoter activities in Pi starvation conditions.
source: In agreement with these findings, our GUS reporter lines show slightly reduced VIH1 and VIH2 promoter activities in Pi starvation conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1 showing GUS staining data.

claim: VIH1-mCit and VIH2-mCit fusion proteins under the control of their native promoters are expressed to similar levels in plants grown in different Pi regimes.
source: VIH1-mCit and VIH2-mCit fusion proteins under the control of their native promoters are expressed to similar levels in plants grown in different Pi regimes (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4A showing confocal microscopy and western blot data.

claim: SPX1 and SPX3 accumulate under Pi starvation.
source: while SPX1 and SPX3 accumulate under Pi starvation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4B showing confocal microscopy and western blot data.

claim: PSI marker proteins SPX1 and SPX3 are highly abundant in the vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant background when expressed under Pi repleted conditions.
source: We next introduced pSPX1::SPX1-eGFP and pSPX3::SPX3-eGFP into our vih1-2 vih2-4 double mutant, and found the PSI marker proteins to be highly abundant in the double mutant background when expressed under Pi repleted conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2 showing confocal microscopy data.

claim: A pPHR1::eGFP-PHR1 control line did not show increased abundance in vih1-2 vih2-4 background under Pi repleted conditions.
source: A pPHR1::eGFP-PHR1 control line did not show this behavior (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Expression of wild-type HsPPIP5K2 or HsPPIP5K2KD/AA carrying point-mutations that target the kinase domain, did not rescue the vih1-2 vih2-4 mutant phenotype.
source: We found that expression of wild-type HsPPIP5K2 or HsPPIP5K2KD/AA carrying point-mutations that target the kinase domain, did not rescue the vih1-2 vih2-4 mutant phenotype (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 3 showing complementation data.

claim: Expression of a HsPPIP5K2RH/AA mutant in the phosphatase domain partially complemented the vih1-2 vih2-4 growth phenotype and restored cellular Pi levels.
source: Notably, expression of a HsPPIP5K2RH/AA mutant in the phosphatase domain partially complemented the vih1-2 vih2-4 growth phenotype (Figure 4C), and restored cellular Pi levels (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4C and 4D showing complementation data.

claim: Human and plant PPIP5Ks may generate similar PP-InsP signaling molecules, able to regulate Pi homeostasis in these different organisms.
source: This indicates that human and plant PPIP5Ks may generate similar PP-InsP signaling molecules, able to regulate Pi homeostasis in these different organisms (Gu et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the complementation data, supported by citation.

claim: VIH enzyme activity is not simply controlled at the transcript or protein level, but most likely through the enzymatic activity of their kinase and phosphatase domains.
source: Together, these experiments indicate that VIH enzyme activity is not simply controlled at the transcript or protein level, but most likely through the enzymatic activity of their kinase and phosphatase domains.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from expression and protein level data.

claim: AtVIH2-KD catalyzes the synthesis of 1PP-InsP5 from InsP6 and InsP8 from 5PP-InsP5.
source: In our assays, we found that AtVIH2-KD catalyzes the synthesis of 1PP-InsP5 from InsP6 and InsP8 from 5PP-InsP5 (Figure 5A,B; Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5A, 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2 showing NMR data.

claim: Human PPIP5K2 catalyzes the synthesis of 1PP-InsP5 from InsP6 and InsP8 from 5PP-InsP5.
source: We recorded similar activities for human PPIP5K2 (Figure 5A,B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1), in agreement with earlier reports (Choi et al., 2007; Fridy et al., 2007; Lin et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with reference to NMR data and citations to previous work.

claim: The AtVIH2-KDKD/AA mutant protein shows no detectable activity using InsP6 as a substrate, and a minuscule activity towards 5PP-InsP5.
source: The AtVIH2-KDKD/AA mutant protein (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) shows no detectable activity using InsP6 as a substrate, and a minuscule activity towards 5PP-InsP5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 2 showing NMR data.

claim: NMR-derived enzyme kinetics suggest 5PP-InsP5 to represent a better substrate for AtVIH2 when compared to InsP6.
source: NMR-derived enzyme kinetics suggest 5PP-InsP5 to represent a better substrate for AtVIH2 when compared to InsP6 (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2 showing kinetic data.

claim: The Arabidopsis VIH kinase domains generate InsP8.
source: Together with the in planta observation that InsP8 levels are reduced and InsP7 levels are increased in vih1-2 vih2-4 mutant seedling (Figure 3E–G), our data reveal that the Arabidopsis VIH kinase domains generate InsP8 .
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from in vitro enzyme assays and in vivo metabolite data.

claim: VIH2 phosphatase domain (VIH2-PD) hydrolyzes both 1PP-InsP5 and 5PP-InsP5, yielding InsP6, but not the non-hydrolyzable 5PCP-InsP5 analog.
source: The VIH2 phosphatase domain recombinantly expressed and purified from insect cells (VIH2-PD, residues 359–1002, Figure 5—figure supplement 1) hydrolyzes both 1PP-InsP5 and 5PP-InsP5, yielding InsP6, but not the non-hydrolyzable 5PCP-InsP5 analog (Figure 5D,E) (Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5D and 5E showing phosphatase assay data.

claim: The Saccharomyces cerevisiae Vip1 phosphatase domain (ScVip1-PD) showed a very similar substrate specificity to VIH2-PD in gel-based assays.
source: The Saccharomyces cerevisiae Vip1 phosphatase domain (ScVip1-PD, residues 515–1088) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), which shares only 24% sequence identity with the plant enzyme (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), showed a very similar substrate specificity in gel-based assays (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5D and 5E showing phosphatase assay data.

claim: Specific 1-phosphatase activity has been previously reported for the isolated Asp1 phosphatase domain from Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
source: It is of note that specific 1-phosphatase activity has been previously reported for the isolated Asp1 phosphatase domain from Schizosaccharomyces pombe (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Wang et al., 2015.

claim: Addition of either magnesium ions or a metal chelator had no detectable effect on VIH2 phosphatase activity during overnight incubation.
source: Addition of either magnesium ions or a metal chelator had no detectable effect on VIH2 phosphatase activity during overnight incubation (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5E showing phosphatase assay data.

claim: Both VIH2-PDRH/AA and ScVip1-PDRH/AA still possess catalytic activity towards the 5PP-InsP7 substrate.
source: We found both VIH2-PDRH/AA and ScVip1-PDRH/AA to still possess catalytic activity towards the 5PP-InsP7 substrate (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 3 showing phosphatase assay data.

claim: The C-terminus of the bifunctional plant and yeast PPIP5K enzymes can hydrolyze different PP-InsP isoforms, but not InsP6.
source: Together, our in vitro assays of the isolated phosphatase domains suggest that the C-terminus of the bifunctional plant and yeast PPIP5K enzymes can hydrolyze different PP-InsP isoforms, but not InsP6.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from in vitro phosphatase assays.

claim: The VIH2RH/AA mutant may still possess residual phosphatase activity in vivo.
source: In addition, the VIH2RH/AA mutant may still possess residual phosphatase activity in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the in vitro data.

claim: At low ATP concentrations the ScVip1 phosphatase activity predominates, releasing InsP6.
source: We found that at low ATP concentrations the ScVip1 phosphatase activity predominates, releasing InsP6 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6A showing gel-based activity assays.

claim: Increasing ATP levels resulted in stimulation of the PP-InsP kinase activity, producing increasing amounts of InsP8.
source: Increasing ATP levels resulted in stimulation of the PP-InsP kinase activity, producing increasing amounts of InsP8 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6A showing gel-based activity assays.

claim: At intermediate ATP concentrations, the kinase and phosphatase activities appear balanced, as no net production of either InsP6 or InsP8 was observed.
source: Interestingly, at intermediate ATP concentrations, the kinase and phosphatase activities appear balanced, as we did not observe net production of either InsP6 or InsP8 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6A showing gel-based activity assays.

claim: Low ATP-Mg2+ concentrations correlate with high ScVIP1 phosphatase activity, and vice versa.
source: We found low ATP-Mg2+ concentrations to correlate with high ScVIP1 phosphatase activity, and vice versa (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6B showing NMR quantification data.

claim: PPIP5K enzymes may relay changes in cellular ATP concentration to changes in PP-InsP levels.
source: Our results suggest that PPIP5K enzymes may relay changes in cellular ATP concentration to changes in PP-InsP levels, as previously reported for the human enzyme (Gu et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from in vitro enzyme assays, supported by citation.

claim: ATP/ADP ratios increased after Pi re-feeding over a 48 hr time course, and were significantly higher when compared to the 0 mM Pi control.
source: We found, that ATP/ADP ratios increased after Pi re-feeding over a 48 hr time course, and were significantly higher when compared to the 0 mM Pi control (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6D showing ATP/ADP measurements.

claim: ATP/ADP ratios did not increase when using 0.5 mM Phi instead of Pi in the re-feeding experiment.
source: Importantly, this was not the case when we used 0.5 mM Phi instead of Pi in the experiment (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6D showing ATP/ADP measurements.

claim: Upon Pi re-feeding plants showed significantly increased fresh weight, root length and cellular Pi content.
source: We confirmed that the conditions chosen for this experiment were physiological relevant and found that upon Pi re-feeding plants showed significantly increased fresh weight, root length and cellular Pi content (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6F showing physiological measurements.

claim: The Pi content was significantly increased compared to the 0 mM Pi control already at 8 hr after re-feeding, while significant differences in seedling fresh weight and root length became apparent after 48 hr.
source: The Pi content was significantly increased compared to the 0 mM Pi control already at 8 hr after re-feeding, while significant differences in seedling fresh weight and root length became apparent after 48 hr (Figure 6C,F).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6C and 6F showing time course data.

claim: No increase in fresh weight, root length or Pi content was observed when using 0.5 mM Phi instead of Pi, despite both molecules suppressing PSI gene expression.
source: No such effect was observed when using 0.5 mM Phi instead of Pi (Figure 6C,F), despite both molecules suppressing PSI gene expression (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6C, 6E and 6F showing physiological and gene expression data.

claim: 5PP-InsP5 hydrolysis by the isolated ScVip1 phosphatase domain is inhibited in the presence of 10 mM Pi in quantitative NMR time course experiments.
source: We found that 5PP-InsP5 hydrolysis by the isolated ScVip1 phosphatase domain is inhibited in the presence of 10 mM Pi in quantitative NMR time course experiments (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2 showing NMR data.

claim: Addition of Pi or Phi promoted the synthesis of InsP8 by full-length ScVip1.
source: We found that addition of Pi or Phi promoted the synthesis of InsP8, which based on our in vivo and in vitro analyses represents the active signaling molecule in plant Pi homeostasis and starvation responses (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2 showing NMR data.

claim: Phi may suppress PSI gene expression by stimulating the kinase activities of VIH1 and VIH2, even though the cellular ATP/ADP ratio remains relatively constant.
source: Thus, Phi may suppress PSI gene expression by stimulating the kinase activities of VIH1 and VIH2, even though the cellular ATP/ADP ratio remains relatively constant (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the enzyme assay and ATP/ADP data.

claim: In physiologically relevant growth conditions, Pi and ATP/ADP levels may together shape the output of the Pi starvation response, by controlling the synthesis and breakdown of the InsP8 signaling molecule catalyzed by VIH1 and VIH2.
source: In physiologically relevant growth conditions, Pi and ATP/ADP levels may together shape the output of the Pi starvation response, by controlling the synthesis and breakdown of the InsP8 signaling molecule catalyzed by VIH1 and VIH2.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Deletion of inositol hexakisphosphate kinases 1 and 2 from human cells, which blocks synthesis of InsP7 and InsP8 isoforms, lead to elevated cellular Pi levels.
source: It is of note that deletion of inositol hexakisphosphate kinases 1 and 2 from human cells, which blocks synthesis of InsP7 and InsP8 isoforms, also lead to elevated cellular Pi levels (Wilson et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Wilson et al., 2019.

claim: Cellular ATP levels are lower in Arabidopsis seedling grown under Pi deficient when compared to Pi replete conditions.
source: We found cellular ATP levels to be lower in Arabidopsis seedling grown under Pi deficient when compared to Pi replete conditions (Figure 6D), in good agreement with what has been reported in other plant species, and in other organisms (Duff et al., 1989; Choi et al., 2017; Gu et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6D and citations to previous work.

claim: At low ATP-Mg2+ levels, Vip1 mainly acts as PP-InsP phosphatase, while at higher ATP-Mg2+ concentrations significant InsP8 synthesis could be observed.
source: Indeed, we found that at low ATP-Mg2+ levels, Vip1 mainly acts as PP-InsP phosphatase, while at higher ATP-Mg2+ concentrations significant InsP8 synthesis could be observed (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6A and 6B showing enzyme assay data.

claim: Eukaryotic diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases/phosphatases have evolved to precisely sense cytosolic ATP concentration, or ATP/ADP ratios, relating changes in Pi levels to changes in PP-InsP pools.
source: We thus speculate that eukaryotic diphosphoinositol pentakisphosphate kinases/phosphatases have evolved to precisely sense cytosolic ATP concentration, or ATP/ADP ratios, relating changes in Pi levels to changes in PP-InsP pools.
evidence: This is stated as speculation based on the enzyme kinetic data.

claim: Pi is an inhibitor of the PPIP5K phosphatase activity.
source: Using the isolated phosphatase and full-length ScVip1, we further characterized Pi as an inhibitor of the phosphatase activity, while promoting InsP8 synthesis in the context of the full-length enzyme (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2 showing enzyme assay data.

claim: PPIP5Ks are subject to complex regulation in vivo.
source: This points to a complex regulation of PPIP5Ks in vivo, which merits further exploration in the future.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the enzyme kinetic data.

claim: Phi stimulates InsP8 synthesis by full-length ScVip1 to a similar extend as the Pi control.
source: Indeed, we found Phi to stimulate InsP8 synthesis by full-length ScVip1 to a similar extend as the Pi control (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2 showing NMR data.

claim: InsP8 is generated and broken down by VIH1/VIH2 in response to changing concentrations of ATP and Pi, to maintain Pi homeostasis and to trigger Pi starvation responses via their SPX domain receptors.
source: Taken together, our findings support a signaling cascade in which InsP8 is generated and broken down by VIH1/VIH2 in response to changing concentrations of ATP and Pi, to maintain Pi homeostasis and to trigger Pi starvation responses via their SPX domain receptors.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from all the data presented.
